newsitem.title: UK: Cherie Blair tastes life in the limelight.
newsitem.headline: Cherie Blair tastes life in the limelight.

text.p: Cherie Blair must be wondering what has hit her after her husband Tony's landslide victory in Britain's general election last week.

She survived the long election campaign by sticking supportively by the side of the man who was to become prime minister and saying absolutely nothing that might damage his chances of ending Labour's 18 long years of opposition.

Now, as the British media scrutinise the handover of power from the old Conservatives to Blair's New Labour, Cherie, a 42-year-old lawyer and mother of three, finds herself under the spotlight as never before.

Tabloid newspapers on Tuesday printed pictures of removal men struggling to carry Cherie's collection of designer shoes out of the couple's fashionable north London home en route to their new residence in Downing Street.
"Who would have guessed Mrs Blair had 50 pairs of shoes to take with her -- including white stacked stilettoes?" wondered the Daily Mail.
After weeks of desperately trying to avoid being dubbed Britain's Hillary Clinton, Cherie found herself being compared unflatteringly with Imelda Marcos.

And after weeks in which fashion commentators had picked over, not always favourably, her choices of elegant designer suits for the campaign trail, the blue track suit she chose for moving house was also given the fashion thumbs-down.
This followed hard on an early-morning media moment at the weekend when Cherie must have wished the earth could have opened up and swallowed her.
With her usually neatly coiffed hair standing up on end and dressed in a nightshirt that revealed rather too much leg, a sleepy-looking Cherie opened her front door to a man delivering flowers.
She shut it quickly enough when she realised to her horror that the episode was being gleefully recorded by massed ranks of cameramen across the street.
All this must be particularly galling for a woman who as a successful lawyer earns twice as much as her husband's prime ministerial salary and who may well become a High Court judge.
With Labour's thumping majority seemingly ensuring a long run in office for her husband, it will be what she has to get used to for years to come.
But she hopes the same will not apply to her children -- Euan, 13, Nicholas, 11, and Kathryn, nine. The Blairs have pleaded with the media to leave them alone to lead as normal a life as possible.
